newsitem.title: CANADA: Magnesium demand to double in coming years - Noranda.
newsitem.headline: Magnesium demand to double in coming years - Noranda.

text.p: Magnesium consumption is expected to grow sharply over the coming years, reaching almost double current levels, largely due to demand in the auto sector, Michael Avedesian of Noranda Metallurgy Inc said.
"I believe that the greatest barrier to growth is on the supply side. You need a long term secure supply at affordable price," Avedesian told Reuters.
"I believe that magnesium demand will grow at five percent per annum until at least 2005," he added.
Avedesian was attending the World Magnesium Conference here.
He expected consumption of magnesium to rise from about 300,000 tonnes a year globally at present to 500,000 tonnes in 2005.

Noranda has poured its first magnesium from a pilot plant earlier this year, and will break ground in April 1998 on a C$700 million new Magnola Metallurgy magnesium joint venture plant which will produce 58,000 tonnes a year from the Fall of 2000, Avedesian said.
"We think we will be very cost competitive," Avedesian said.
Noranda has a 52 percent stake in Magnola, with Aisin Seiki of Japan holding 16 percent. Aisin is 24 percent owned by Toyota Motor Corp.
Aisin makes car components, a key growth sector for the light metal.
